newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF PRAISES BULGARIAN REFORM PERFORMANCE.
newsitem.headline: IMF PRAISES BULGARIAN REFORM PERFORMANCE.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund praised Bulgaria's reform performance in the first review of its stand-by agreement but recommended a tougher approach on liquidations and bank restructuring, the government said.

"The majority of IMF executive directors praised Bulgarian authorities for the restoration of confidence in the national currency and financial institutions, which was more rapid than expected," the press centre said in a statement.

The statement, in Bulgarian, quoted a letter to Bulgaria's finance minister and central bank governor from the IMF executive director for the group of countries including Bulgaria, Johannes Wijndholds.
The IMF on Wednesday approved the release of a $130 million second tranche of a 14-month $510 million stand-by approved in April.
"The IMF pointed out the considerable rise in foreign exchange reserves and the favourable developments concerning inflation and interest rate targets," said the statement.

"The IMF recommended to Bulgaria to follow a more aggressive approach towards the process of liquidation and financial isolation of loss-making enterprises and towards rehabilitation and privatisation of state banks," it said.

Bulgarian National Bank Issue Department foreign exchange reserves rose to 3.2 billion marks on July 18 from 2.8 billion marks on July 1 when Bulgaria introduced a restrictive fixed exchange rate system known as a currency board.
Monthly inflation slowed to 0.8 percent in June from 5.6 percent in May as financial stabilisation took hold.
The central bank announced another cut in its main lev interest rate to 5.42 percent annually from 6.12 percent from Monday. The main rate stood at 18 percent monthly in March.
The IMF also said it was was encouraged by Bulgaria's efforts to improve the business climate through a campaign against crime and corruption. -- Sofia newsroom +359-2 981 4145
